question: What are the best alternatives to LinkedIn Learning for enterprise upskilling?
text:
If you're evaluating LinkedIn Learning for enterprise-wide upskilling, I'd shortlist these five. The best choice depends heavily on whether your priority is broad workforce learning, technical depth, credentials, or hands-on practice.

Platform	Best for	Compared with LinkedIn Learning
Coursera	Enterprise reskilling + recognized credentials	Stronger credentials and academic depth
Udemy Business	Broad, practical skills at scale	Broader practical catalog; very strong for fast-moving skills
Pluralsight	Engineering, cloud, AI & cybersecurity	Much deeper technical assessment and hands-on practice
O'Reilly	Engineering + professional/technical teams	Deeper technical reference material and expert content
Skillsoft	Large-enterprise L&D, compliance & leadership	Stronger traditional enterprise-L&D capabilities
1. Coursera — best overall for strategic reskilling

Coursera for Business

I'd choose Coursera if you're trying to move beyond "employees watch courses" toward structured workforce transformation.

It combines courses from universities and companies, Professional Certificates, role-specific learning paths and enterprise analytics. Coursera currently says its business catalog includes 10,600+ courses, 1,400+ specializations and 165+ Professional Certificates, with content from 350+ companies and universities. 
C
Coursera
+1

Best for: AI/data transformation, business skills, digital transformation, professional credentials.

Weakness: Less compelling than Pluralsight or O'Reilly for engineers who need very deep technical material and hands-on environments.

2. Udemy Business — best broad alternative

Udemy Business

Udemy Business is probably the closest substitute if what you like about LinkedIn Learning is the enormous range of immediately usable courses.

Its enterprise offering now has 30,000+ courses, spanning technology, business, leadership, compliance and AI, with assessments, learning paths, analytics and AI-powered learning features. 
U
Udemy Business
+1

Best for: Large heterogeneous workforces where engineers, salespeople, managers, HR and other functions all need different training.

Weakness: The enormous marketplace-style catalog can require more curation to ensure consistently high-quality learning paths.

3. Pluralsight — best for technology organizations

Pluralsight Enterprise

If your main objective is technical upskilling, I'd put Pluralsight ahead of LinkedIn Learning.

It combines courses with skill/role assessments, 3,500+ hands-on labs, cloud and AI sandboxes, certification preparation and technical learning paths. Its enterprise platform also supports SSO, APIs, LMS integrations and advanced analytics. 
P
Pluralsight

This becomes particularly attractive for organizations undergoing cloud migration, AI adoption or software modernization. Pluralsight launched its Cloud Ready program in 2026 specifically around cloud and AI workforce readiness. 
P
Pluralsight

Best for: Software engineering, DevOps, cloud, cybersecurity, data and AI.

Weakness: Less suitable as a single platform for broad nontechnical workforce development.

4. O'Reilly — best for serious technical teams

O'Reilly Learning

O'Reilly is particularly strong when your learners are developers, architects, data scientists, IT professionals and technical leaders.

Its differentiator isn't just video courses: its library includes books, videos, live events, courses and labs. O'Reilly says its platform contains 75,000+ titles from nearly 200 publishers. 
O
O'Reilly Media

Best for: Engineering organizations that want a technical knowledge platform rather than primarily a video-course library.

Weakness: Not as natural a fit for company-wide soft-skills and general professional development.

5. Skillsoft — best for traditional enterprise L&D

Skillsoft is worth considering if your buying criteria include leadership development, compliance, business skills, certifications and enterprise L&D administration alongside technical learning.

I'd particularly investigate it if you're replacing LinkedIn Learning in a large, established organization where L&D governance, reporting and structured programs matter as much as the content itself.

My recommendation

I'd narrow it down like this:

Platform	Best for	Compared with LinkedIn Learning
Coursera	Enterprise reskilling + recognized credentials	Stronger credentials and academic depth
Udemy Business	Broad, practical skills at scale	Broader practical catalog; very strong for fast-moving skills
Pluralsight	Engineering, cloud, AI & cybersecurity	Much deeper technical assessment and hands-on practice
O'Reilly	Engineering + professional/technical teams	Deeper technical reference material and expert content
Skillsoft	Large-enterprise L&D, compliance & leadership	Stronger traditional enterprise-L&D capabilities

One important distinction: don't compare these primarily by course count. For an enterprise purchase, I'd score them on skills taxonomy/assessment, role-based paths, content freshness, hands-on practice, credentials, integrations/SSO, analytics, proprietary-content support, localization, AI learning capabilities, and—most importantly—evidence that learning translates into job skills.

If you tell me your employee count, main skill areas (e.g. AI/software/business/leadership), geography, and approximate budget per employee, I can make a shortlist of 2–3 platforms with an enterprise buying matrix and estimated total cost.
